sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or give reasons).

questions.q: Match Column A and Column B. A: (1) ISI mark (2) Green dot on label (3) Agmark (4) Red dot on label. B: (a) Ghee and honey (b) Gas cylinder (c) Non-vegetarian foods (d) Vegetarian foods.
State True or False. (a) Children are not consumers. (b) Room coolers and fans should be bought preferably in winter or off-season.
questions.answer: (a) False: everyone is a consumer. (b) True.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The MRP is the ________ price at which a product is sold. (b) Products bearing ________ marks are of a certain minimum quality.
Match the rights. (a) Choosing among Lotus, Bata and Adidas shoes (b) Complaining about a faulty immersion rod and wanting replacement. Options: right to be heard, to choose, to redressal.
questions.answer: (a) Right to choose. (b) Right to redressal.

questions.q: Write the standardisation mark usually found on each: (i) paint (ii) honey (iii) canned juice (iv) pure wool shawl.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Enumerate the six consumer rights.
questions.answer: Right to safety, to be informed, to choose, to be heard, to redressal and to consumer education.

questions.q: Explain the importance of labels and markings on textile or food products.
questions.answer: A label gives the name, ingredients, net weight, MRP, expiry date and directions. It helps consumers make informed choices and avoid unsafe or low-quality products.

questions.q: List any two problems faced by consumers and suggest a solution for each.
questions.answer: Adulteration: buy packed, labelled and standard-marked goods. Defective weights: be vigilant and refuse irregular weights, reporting such shops.

questions.q: What is consumer education?
questions.answer: It educates consumers about what, where, when, how and how much to buy and how to use the goods bought.

questions.q: Name any two laws for consumer protection.
questions.answer: The Consumer Protection Act and the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (also the BIS Act and AGMARK Act).

questions.q: What is the Eco Mark?
questions.answer: It is a mark launched in 1991 and given by BIS to products that meet ISI standards and are environment friendly.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Enumerate the six consumer rights as defined under the Consumer Protection Act. Explain any one in detail.
questions.answer: (i) Rights: safety, to be informed, to choose, to be heard, to redressal and consumer education. (ii) Right to safety protects against products and services harmful to life and property, such as adulterated food and unsafe electrical appliances. (iii) Hence products must be safe and carry standard marks.

or.q: List any five common problems faced by consumers in the market. Suggest solutions for any two.
or.answer: (i) Price variation, adulteration, hoarding and black marketing, defective weights and deceptive trade practices. (ii) For adulteration, buy standard-marked packed goods from reliable shops. (iii) For defective weights, insist on correct weights and report cheating.

questions.q: Explain the advantages of consumer education (three points).
questions.answer: (i) It develops the ability to decide and choose intelligently. (ii) It helps to demand safe, reliable and good quality products at reasonable prices. (iii) It makes consumers alert against corrupt practices and ready to take action.

questions.q: Explain the responsibilities of a consumer (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Take bills and guarantee cards and keep them safe as proof. (ii) Insist on standardised goods and do not be carried away by sales talk or free gifts. (iii) Follow instructions, report cheating and do not waste products.

questions.q: Explain how the consumer movement helps consumers (three points).
questions.answer: (i) It makes consumers aware of their rights and responsibilities. (ii) It helps them to report wrong practices and seek redressal. (iii) It lets them share information and represent consumer interests to the Government.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the problems faced by consumers and the solutions to them.
questions.answer: (i) Price variation and overcharging: compare prices, buy from reliable shops and check MRP. (ii) Adulteration and poor quality: buy packed and labelled goods with ISI, AGMARK or FPO marks. (iii) Hoarding and black marketing: refuse to pay more and report. (iv) Defective weights and measures: reject irregular weights and check the scale. (v) Deceptive trade practices and poor guidance: do a market survey and avoid sales tricks. (vi) Keep bills and guarantee cards and report cheating to the authorities.
